open-question.question: Where should the macOS build script live, and what should it be called? The repo has no scripts/ directory or app build script yet. Options include a repo-root scripts/build-macos.sh, a script inside flutter/, or something else.
open-question.alternative: Create a new top-level `scripts/` directory and put the script there as `scripts/build-macos.sh`. It resolves the repo root from its own location, then runs `mopro build` at the root and `flutter build macos` inside `flutter/`. This starts a repo-level convention in a repo that has none yet. A future `scripts/build-linux.sh` or a Windows/WSL script fits beside it with matching names. The script also sits at the level where its first step (`mopro build`, driven by the root `Config.toml`) runs and where the three version files it compares (`Cargo.toml`, `flutter/pubspec.yaml`, `mopro_flutter_bindings/rust/Cargo.toml`) are equally reachable. It adds a new top-level directory holding a single file. The generic "build" name also hides the fact that the script signs and packages a dmg as well as building. That may be a problem next to future scripts, unless those scripts follow the same build-plus-package pattern.

Put the script in the Flutter project, as `flutter/build-macos.sh` or `flutter/scripts/build-macos.sh`, so it lives next to `flutter/macos/` and the `flutter build` it runs. It sits beside the app it packages, where `Release.entitlements`, `AppInfo.xcconfig` and `flutter/build/macos/Build/Products/Release` are. It also matches the "Build from Source" section of `docs/Linux.md`, which already tells people to `cd flutter` before building. The script's first step, `mopro build`, has to run from the repo root and regenerates the `mopro_flutter_bindings/` bindings, and it checks `Cargo.toml` versions outside `flutter/`. So a script inside `flutter/` has to climb out of its own directory for its main work, which makes it look narrower than it is. It also places a repo-wide release tool inside a subproject whose `build/` directory is git-ignored and removed by `flutter clean`, which makes a misplaced path an easy mistake.

Put the script directly in the repo root, next to `Cargo.toml` and `Config.toml`, with a name that says what it produces, e.g. `build-macos-dmg.sh` or `release-macos.sh`. It is the easiest place to find: it shows up with `ls` next to the README, it needs no new directory, and it follows the pattern the repo already has of a runnable `.sh` at the top level of the tree it works on (e.g. `groth16-prover-min/build-circuit.sh`, `claim-relayer/e2e-anvil/run.sh`). A name like `build-macos-dmg.sh` also states the output clearly. It clutters a root that already holds the mopro crate files (`build.rs`, `Config.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), where a stray shell script can look like part of the Rust/mopro build. It also sets no pattern for more platform scripts, so a later Linux or Windows packaging script would either pile up at the root or force a move to `scripts/`.

open-question.question: Where should the script write the final .dmg and its intermediate staging files? For example, a git-ignored dist/ directory at the repo root, or somewhere under flutter/build/. Should an existing output be overwritten or should the script refuse?
open-question.alternative: Write the final dmg to a new `dist/` directory at the repo root, and add a new `dist/` entry to the root `.gitignore` because nothing ignores it today. Build the dmg staging folder (the `.app` copy and the `/Applications` symlink) in a `mktemp -d` directory that is deleted by an exit `trap`. Silently replace any existing dmg of the same name. The output is easy to find and separate from all build state. A `flutter clean` or removing `flutter/build/` never deletes a finished release dmg. Staging in a temp directory means a failed run leaves no half-built staging tree behind. Re-running for the same version just works, which suits a build → sign → dmg dry run repeated until it passes. It adds a new top-level directory and a `.gitignore` change. Silent overwrite can replace a dmg whose SHA-256 was already published on a GitHub release. If the same version is rebuilt, the new file's checksum will differ from the published one, and nothing warns about it.

Use the same git-ignored repo-root `dist/` for the final dmg and a temp directory for staging. If the target dmg already exists, the script stops with an error before doing any build work, unless a flag such as `--force` is passed to allow overwriting. A dmg whose checksum may already be on a GitHub release is never replaced by accident. The versioned file name makes a name clash mean exactly "this version was already packaged", so refusing is a meaningful safeguard. Checking up front also avoids wasting a long `mopro build` / `flutter build macos` run. It adds a flag and a code path to the script. Repeated dry runs of the same version need `--force` or a manual delete every time, which gets in the way during this milestone's fix-until-it-passes loop. How often this bites depends on how the version-naming question settles.

Put both the staging folder and the final dmg under the Flutter build tree, for example `flutter/build/macos/dmg/`, next to the `Build/Products/Release` app it packages. Replace existing output freely because it is a disposable build product. It needs no new directory and no `.gitignore` change, because the root and `flutter/.gitignore` `build/` patterns already cover it. It keeps every artifact of one build in one place, next to the `.app` it came from. The dmg is hidden deep in a build tree, and it is lost whenever that tree is wiped. `flutter clean` deletes all of `flutter/build/`, so if the clean-build policy runs a clean at the start of each build, the previous release dmg disappears without warning. Nothing marks it apart from the intermediate files.

Write both staging and the final dmg to a directory under a repo-root `build/`, for example `build/macos/`, which the root `.gitignore`'s existing `build/` pattern already ignores. Replace existing output on each run. The output sits at the top level where it is easy to find. It needs no `.gitignore` edit. It is outside the Flutter project, so `flutter clean` does not touch it. A root `build/` next to cargo's `target/` suggests an intermediate build tree rather than a release deliverable. Keeping staging and the final dmg in the same place makes it easier to confuse or accidentally delete the finished artifact. Silent overwrite has the same risk of changing an already-published checksum.

open-question.question: Which file is the authoritative version for the dmg file name and the bundle's CFBundleShortVersionString? Candidates are the root Cargo.toml (currently 0.5.1) and flutter/pubspec.yaml (currently 0.5.0). What should the script do when they disagree, given that it only warns?
open-question.alternative: The script reads the version from flutter/pubspec.yaml (currently 0.5.0) and uses it for the dmg file name. It runs flutter build macos without overriding the version, so CFBundleShortVersionString comes from FLUTTER_BUILD_NAME as Info.plist already does. If the root Cargo.toml or the bindings dependency disagrees, the script prints a warning naming both values and carries on. No build flags are needed, and the name and bundle always agree. The dmg name, the About/Finder version and the pubspec are the same value because Flutter already takes it from the pubspec. With the repo as it is, the first build is 0.5.0 even though the latest tag is v0.5.1 and Cargo.toml says 0.5.1. Unless the pubspec is bumped first, the release is published under an older version than it contains. Fixing that mismatch is out of scope for this milestone.

The script reads the version from the root Cargo.toml (currently 0.5.1, which matches the latest tag and the bindings dependency). It uses that version for the dmg name and passes it to flutter build macos --build-name, so it overrides the pubspec in CFBundleShortVersionString. If pubspec.yaml disagrees, the script warns and says the pubspec value was overridden. With the repo as it is, this gives the correct 0.5.1 in both the file name and the bundle. It also follows the two files CLAUDE.md already requires to match (the root Cargo.toml and the bindings dependency), with no need to fix the pubspec first. The bundle's version no longer comes from the pubspec, so a plain flutter build macos made by hand gives a different CFBundleShortVersionString than the script does. Anyone who bumps only the pubspec later is quietly overridden, and a warning is the only sign.

The maintainer passes the release version on the command line, or the script takes it from the git tag at HEAD (for example v0.5.1 without the "v"). The script uses it for the dmg name and passes it as --build-name. It checks it against Cargo.toml, the bindings dependency and pubspec.yaml, and warns about each file that differs. The version stays tied to the release tag being published instead of to either file, so the mismatch neither file can settle on its own does not choose the name. Every file that disagrees is reported the same way. It adds a required input or a dependency on the git state. A build without a tag or without the argument needs a fallback rule, which brings back the question of which file wins. The bundle version can also differ from both files, which is confusing when someone looks at the build later.

open-question.question: What exact naming convention should the dmg file and its mounted volume use? The Linux release uses zkp-migration-app-linux-amd64.tar.gz with no version. Should the macOS file follow the same pattern with a version added (e.g. zkp-migration-app-macos-arm64-<version>.dmg)? What volume name should users see when they open it?

Xcode already ad-hoc signs the Release build with Release.entitlements (app-sandbox and network.client), but codesign --force --deep -s - without --entitlements removes them. Should the script re-sign explicitly with flutter/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements, keep Xcode's signature and only verify it, or do something else? Should the app stay sandboxed?

Should the script always run mopro build (which regenerates the committed Dart bindings and can leave the working tree dirty), make it optional with a flag, or skip it by default? If mopro-cli is missing, should the script just fail with install instructions or install it automatically?

Which prerequisites should the script check before building, and how strict should each check be? Candidates: host is arm64 macOS, Xcode command-line tools, flutter, CocoaPods, cargo/rustup with the aarch64-apple-darwin target, mopro, hdiutil/codesign/shasum, a clean git working tree, and building on a release tag or branch. Which of these fail the build and which only warn?

Should the script always start from a clean build (e.g. flutter clean and removing the previous Release products) so release artifacts are reproducible? Or should it reuse incremental build state for speed, perhaps with a flag to choose?

Which checks should the script run after building, and what counts as success? For example: codesign --verify --deep --strict on the app, checking the entitlements are present, hdiutil verify on the dmg, a test mount, and spctl --assess. spctl is expected to reject an ad-hoc-signed app, so should it be reported for information only?

Should the script only print the dmg's SHA-256, or also write it to a sidecar file (e.g. <dmg>.sha256 in shasum format) that can be attached to the GitHub release? Which command should the user doc tell users to run to check it (shasum -a 256)?

Where should the maintainer instructions for the build script live: a --help/usage block in the script, a "Build from source / Release" section in docs/macOS.md like docs/Linux.md has, a separate maintainer doc, or a combination?

Which Gatekeeper workaround(s) should docs/macOS.md document for the unsigned app, given the minimum supported macOS is 12 and recent macOS versions dropped the right-click → Open shortcut? Options: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the installed app, or both. Should the doc explain the "damaged"/"unidentified developer" messages users will see?
Should docs/macOS.md include a screenshot (docs/macos.png) like the Linux and Windows guides? Should any existing doc (e.g. the root README.md or flutter/README.md) link to the new macOS guide?
